summary: Klaus Bruhn was an Indologist who studied at the University of Hamburg under Ludwig Alsdorf and Walther Schubring, completing his Dr. phil. and Habilitation there. He served as Professor für Indologie at the Free University of Berlin from 1966 to 1991.

Klaus Butzenberger is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He studied at the University of Munich under Friedrich Wilhelm and completed his Habilitation at the Free University of Berlin, later holding the chair at the University of Tübingen (1999–2017).

Klaus Karttunen specializes in Indology, history, and archaeology. He completed his BA through PhD at the University of Helsinki, studying under Pentti Aalto and Asko Parpola, and held positions there including Docent and joint Acting Professor of Indology.

Indologist Klaus Ludwig Janert studied at the University of Halle and Goethe University Frankfurt under Paul Thieme. He served as an assistant at the University of Göttingen before holding a full professorship at the University of Cologne (1963–1987).

Klaus Mylius worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Halle-Wittenberg and the University of Leipzig, later teaching Sanskrit philology at Leipzig (1970–1991) and ancient, middle, and Indo-Aryan languages at Goethe University Frankfurt (1996–2022).
Klaus Pinte works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He studied at Ghent University under Pol Vanden Broucke and served as a teaching assistant there in 2006.

Klaus Röhrborn is a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. After studying at Hamburg, Leipzig, and Giessen, he became a professor at Giessen (1972) and Ordinarius für Turkologie at Göttingen (1992–2003).

Klaus Wille is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He held posts at the University of Göttingen (attested 1996), the Austrian Academy of Sciences (attested 1997), and the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2000–2009 and 2018–2020).

Klaus-Dieter Mathes is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Marburg under Michael Hahn and his Habilitation at Hamburg, later serving as Director of the Nepal-German Manuscript Preservation Project and Professor at Vienna.

Klaus-Josef Notz was a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. He studied theology at Benediktbeuern and the University of Munich, where he earned his Doctor theologiae and later served as a Lehrbeauftragter in 1996.
Klemens Karlsson is a scholar in religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at Uppsala University, completing his Doctor of Philosophy under the supervision of Peter Schalk by 2000.

Knut A. Jacobsen is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He earned his PhD at the University of California, Santa Barbara, and became Professor in the History of Religions at the University of Bergen in 1996.

Kobun Chino Otogawa was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Komazawa University, Kyoto University under Gadjin M. Nagao, and Eihei-ji. He served at the Tassajara Zen Mountain Center, Haiku Zendo, and regularly taught at Naropa University in 2001.

Kodo Akino was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University and under Keido Ito, Gen'ei Kato, and Bokusan Nishiari. He held multiple leadership roles at Komazawa University, becoming president in 1909, and lectured at the University of Tokyo.
Kodo Kawamura was a Buddhist studies scholar who completed his master's and doctorate at Komazawa University, where he also served as a professor from roughly 1965 to 2004.
Kodo Nomura was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and served as a researcher at Taisho University.

Kodo Sawaki was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Senju-ji, Takada Junior College, and Hōryū-ji under several teachers. He served as a professor at Komazawa University (1935–1963) and abbot of Antai-ji (around 1949–1965).
Koen Wellens works in Sinology, Tibetology, and religious studies. He studied at Ghent University under Charles Willemen and completed his PhD at the University of Oslo under Per Kværne.
Koenraad Elst is a scholar of Indology, Sinology, and religious studies. He completed an MA at KU Leuven and studied at Banaras Hindu University.

Kogen Mizuno was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. He earned a doctorate from the University of Tokyo, where he was later a professor (1959–1962), and served as a professor and president (1976) at Komazawa University.
